title: Perform a Lambda version-and-alias release with rollback / Perform a managed EKS Deployment rollout / Perform an EC2 blue/green deployment with CodeDeploy

blocks.text: A published Lambda version freezes function code and most configuration. The alias is movable: it selects a published version for invocations. Use aws lambda publish-version --function-name NAME, then aws lambda update-alias --function-name NAME --name ALIAS --function-version VERSION. Test NAME:ALIAS. For rollback, point the alias at the approved previous version and repeat verification.

blocks.change_summary: The alias target moves; published snapshots do not change.

blocks.text: Record the alias target before release, after release and after rollback. The supplied NAME:ALIAS test checks the version selected by that alias; an unqualified function invocation is not that test.

Rollback changes the alias target, not the immutable published snapshot. Inspect the target and repeat the supplied result check for the approved previous version. A version captures most configuration, not every possible configuration property.

public.prompt: Release record: published versions 7 and 8 retain their original code and configuration snapshots. Alias LIVE initially targets version 7, then targets version 8 after an alias update. Which statement correctly explains this record?

options.text: Rollback edits the code inside the previously published version.
An alias is an immutable snapshot, while the published version is the movable pointer.
The published version is an immutable snapshot; the alias can move between published versions.

o1.message: Rollback moves the alias; it does not rewrite an immutable published snapshot.

o2.message: This reverses the roles: the alias is movable and the version is immutable.

o3.message: The version freezes code and most configuration; the alias selects the invocation target.

public.prompt: Read each Lambda release-and-rollback transcript. Decide whether it verifies both approved alias updates using the alias-qualified test.

buckets.label: Fails at least one stated criterion

items.text: Approved previous: PREVIOUS; approved new: NEW. Version NEW published; ALIAS moves PREVIOUS -> NEW -> PREVIOUS. Both checks invoke unqualified NAME. Record says alias verification complete.

Approved previous: PREVIOUS; new: NEW. Before: ALIAS -> PREVIOUS. After release: ALIAS -> NEW; NAME:ALIAS test confirms NEW. Rollback request accepted; no alias-target observation or post-rollback result check.

Approved previous version: PREVIOUS; approved new version: NEW.
Before: ALIAS -> PREVIOUS.
aws lambda publish-version --function-name NAME
Result: NEW
aws lambda update-alias --function-name NAME --name ALIAS --function-version NEW
After release: ALIAS -> NEW; supplied test invokes NAME:ALIAS; expected NEW result confirmed.
aws lambda update-alias --function-name NAME --name ALIAS --function-version PREVIOUS
After rollback: ALIAS -> PREVIOUS; supplied test invokes NAME:ALIAS; expected PREVIOUS result confirmed.

i1.message: The supplied verification must target NAME:ALIAS; an unqualified invocation does not verify the alias target.

i2.message: Rollback needs the restored target observation and the alias-qualified test result, not only request acceptance.

i3.message: The targets are recorded before, after release and after rollback, with alias-qualified result checks after both updates.

blocks.text: A Deployment Pod-template change creates a rollout revision; scaling alone does not. Update the supplied image with kubectl set image deployment/NAME CONTAINER=IMAGE and monitor kubectl rollout status deployment/NAME. On the controlled failure, inspect rollout history, restore the approved prior revision with kubectl rollout undo deployment/NAME --to-revision=REVISION, and verify readiness.

Post-rollback readiness check — restored Deployment meets the supplied readiness requirement

blocks.text: Keep the failed revision evidence separate from the approved rollback revision. Use the supplied procedure to select the authorized prior revision, rather than choosing an arbitrary history entry.

After undo, inspect readiness. An accepted undo request is not evidence that the restored template’s Pods satisfy the supplied readiness check. Scaling changes alone do not create a new Pod-template revision.

buckets.label: Fails at least one stated criterion

items.text: Supplied image update and status checked. History distinguishes FAILED from approved REVISION. Undo to REVISION accepted. No readiness observation; record says rollback verified.

Supplied target: deployment/NAME, container CONTAINER, image IMAGE.
kubectl set image deployment/NAME CONTAINER=IMAGE
kubectl rollout status deployment/NAME
Controlled failure observed. Supplied history: failed revision FAILED; approved prior revision REVISION.
kubectl rollout undo deployment/NAME --to-revision=REVISION
Restored revision: REVISION. Supplied readiness check: ready.

Image update targets deployment/NAME and CONTAINER=IMAGE; rollout status and history checked. History identifies approved prior REVISION and another unapproved prior OTHER. Undo targets OTHER; readiness reports ready.

i1.message: Acceptance of undo alone is not the required readiness verification.

i2.message: The record targets only the supplied image update, distinguishes revisions, restores the approved revision and verifies readiness.

i3.message: A ready unapproved history entry is not the explicit approved prior revision.

blocks.text: EC2 blue/green installs a revision on replacement instances before traffic leaves the original instances. Use the supplied deployment group, replacement fleet and load balancer configuration. Check lifecycle and health evidence before approved rerouting. For rollback, follow the supplied configuration or redeployment procedure and verify both traffic and application behavior return to the known-good revision.

blocks.text: Installation evidence shows the replacement revision is present; it does not show which fleet clients reach. Preserve lifecycle and health evidence before the approved traffic switch.

After the switch and after rollback, check client-visible behavior as well as traffic. Rerouting alone does not establish correct application behavior. Follow the supplied rollback path; do not infer automatic rollback or guaranteed zero disruption.

public.prompt: Read each EC2 blue/green record. Decide whether it verifies replacement readiness before traffic switching and verifies the traffic, revision and behavior outcomes after switching and rollback.

buckets.label: Fails at least one stated criterion

items.text: Supplied deployment group, replacement fleet and load balancer used. Replacement revision installed; lifecycle passed; health passed before approved traffic switch. After switch: traffic reaches replacement fleet; expected revision and client-visible behavior confirmed. Supplied rollback/redeployment procedure followed. After rollback: traffic reaches procedure-designated known-good destination; known-good revision confirmed; application behavior passes supplied check.

Supplied deployment group, fleet and load balancer used. Traffic switched before replacement lifecycle and health evidence was checked. Afterward health passed. Rollback procedure and final traffic, known-good revision and behavior were verified.

Replacement installation, lifecycle and health verified before approved switch; post-switch traffic, revision and behavior verified. Supplied rollback requested; record contains no post-rollback traffic, revision or behavior observations and calls rollback successful.

i1.message: Installation, lifecycle and health precede switching; separate traffic, revision and behavior evidence verifies both outcomes.

i2.message: Healthy evidence must be verified before the approved switch, not retroactively after rerouting.

i3.message: The request does not verify return of traffic and application behavior to the known-good revision.
